title: AI Fashion Lookbook Photos and Outfit Ads | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one outfit photo into AI lookbook photos of one complete look. Use them on the collection page or a launch ad, and check every layer against stock.
h1: AI Lookbook Photos for One Complete Outfit
lead: Upload one complete outfit for AI lookbook photos. An AI actor can wear the set, and the same photo can carry a voiceover when you make the clip.
steps_h2: Make Fashion Editorial Photos in 3 Steps
steps_lead: Upload the full outfit, name one location and one light, then download the photo for the collection page.

steps.d: Lay the full outfit in one well-lit frame, layers separated. Include the top, bottom, outer layer, and shoes if they are part of it.
Name one location and one kind of light for an editorial still. Repeat that choice across the drop when the set should feel connected.
Check each layer against your stock, then add price and links outside the image. Publish only frames that still match the pieces you can ship.

faq.q: What should the source photo include?
faq.a: Show every piece in the look, including the top, bottom, outer layer, and the shoes or featured accessory, in one frame. If a layer is missing from the source, do not treat the frame as if that piece is there.

faq.q: How do I keep a collection looking connected?
faq.a: Reuse one location, one light, and one crop across looks, and let each garment stay distinct. A digital twin can repeat so the set feels like one shoot. Open with the hero outfit.

faq.q: Can I show more than one outfit in a single image?
faq.a: Use one full look per image so the silhouette stays clear. Make a separate image for the next outfit.

faq.q: Do I need a photographer or models?
faq.a: No. Each lookbook photo is generated from an outfit photo you already have. The person is an AI actor you pick from the actor library, not someone you booked and not a customer.

faq.q: How is this different from hiring a creator?
faq.a: A creator needs samples, a fee, and time on the calendar. Here you upload one photo or paste a product page link, pick a scene, and pay the credits for that job.

faq.q: What does a lookbook photo cost?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits. The cost is shown before you start, and a failed job returns those credits. There is no free plan. The download has no watermark, and you can use it in your own ads, pages, and posts.

faq.q: Can the same scene cover menswear and womenswear?
faq.a: Yes. Menswear lookbook photos and womenswear looks can share a crop and a light when each outfit has its own source photo. Check tailoring and lengths against the garments you sell.

faq.q: Can I use the frames in a launch?
faq.a: Yes. They fit a collection page, a carousel, or a launch email after you add prices yourself. A launch that also needs motion is covered by [product launch video and photos](page:occ-product-launch).

faq.q: Can the look include a voiceover and captions?
faq.a: The lookbook frame is a still. When you make a clip from the same outfit photo, add a voiceover, captions, and a track from the music library, then publish that clip to TikTok or Meta.

faq.q: Can I start from a product link or another language?
faq.a: Yes. Paste a product page link, ask for a short script, and speak the line in another language. A catalog API can start the next look. You see the credit cost before each job.

reviews.h2: Labels Are Switching to AI Lookbook Photos
reviews.lead: Example ways a label builds the set, including menswear lookbook photos and a collection launch lookbook. Check every layer against stock.

items.t: One finished frame from the outfit photo
items.d: Example: a label uploads the full outfit and gets one AI lookbook photo for the collection page. A missing layer is left out of the frame.

items.t: The still and a short clip together
items.d: Example: the shop makes the editorial still and a short outfit clip from the same photo, in one project, on a first try.

items.t: Menswear lookbook photos from a link
items.d: Example: a menswear shop pastes the product page link, or uploads the suit, and keeps jacket, trousers, and shoes in one frame.

items.t: An AI actor, then a trim in the editor
items.d: Example: the label picks an AI actor from the actor library for the hero look, then trims the companion clip and sets captions.

items.t: The same look in another language
items.d: Example: the carousel stays one crop and one light, and the spoken line on the clip is recorded again for a second market.

items.t: Music and a voiceover on the clip
items.d: Example: the lookbook frame stays a still. On the clip, the editor adds a voiceover and a track from the music library.

items.t: An AI actor instead of a fitting day
items.d: Example: a boutique uses an AI actor for the hero outfit. Someone new to photos can start from one flat lay.

items.t: A digital twin across the collection launch lookbook
items.d: Example: a digital twin wears each look so the set feels connected, and each outfit still has its own source photo.

items.t: A script, then a second crop
items.d: Example: the agency pastes the product link, takes a short script, and makes a second crop from the same outfit photo.

items.t: Publish the clip, or start from the API
items.d: Example: after the lengths match stock, the shop publishes the clip to Instagram or TikTok. A catalog API can start the next look.
